---
title: "Reproducibility and Limits"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/common.R")
source("R/params.R")
tr <- read.csv("data/test_results.csv")
ck <- read.csv("data/checksums.csv")
lock <- jsonlite::fromJSON("renv.lock")
ver <- function(p) lock$Packages[[p]]$Version
md5s <- function(f) substr(ck$md5[ck$file == f], 1, 8)
pp <- function(...) par_get(...)
```

## Run it

One command rebuilds everything from seed `r pp("seed")`: the simulation, models, analyses, tests and this site.

```sh
Rscript run_all.R
```

The last run passed `r sum(tr$checks_passed)` checks (`r tr$checks_passed[tr$suite == "simulation"]` simulation, `r tr$checks_passed[tr$suite == "artifacts"]` artifact). Packages
are locked in `renv.lock` (R `r lock$R$Version`; `probcal` `r ver("probcal")`, `forecastdom` `r ver("forecastdom")`, `falsifyr` `r ver("falsifyr")`).
The generator file's checksum is `r md5s("R/simulate.R")`; any edit changes it. Result checksums and the full
session record are in the [source repository](https://github.com/patrick-lefler/rQuarto_three_questions_for_any_risk_model_2026-10-22/tree/main/data).

## What is fixed

Every analysis choice lives in `params.yaml`, which the scripts read. The table shows the main ones.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-params
#| tbl-cap: "Main analysis settings and their basis. The full register, with sensitivity ranges, is in params.yaml."
w <- function(n) paste(range(pp("windows", n)), collapse = "–")
tab <- data.frame(
  Setting = c("Random seed", "Windows: classifier / overlay fit / overlay test",
              "Score sharpening", "Risk-band boundaries", "Resampling draws",
              "Trimming rule", "Deletion budget", "Significance level"),
  Value = c(pp("seed"), sprintf("%s / %s / %s", w("classifier_train"), w("calibration_fit"), w("overlay_eval")),
            pp("vendorscore", "sharpen"), sprintf("%s, %s", pct(pp("calibration", "band_low_upper"), 0), pct(pp("calibration", "band_medium_upper"), 0)),
            format(pp("calibration", "bootstrap_draws"), big.mark = ","), sprintf("top %s of patch latency", pct(1 - pp("fragility", "trim_percentile"), 0)),
            pp("fragility", "deletion_budget"), pct(pp("fragility", "alpha"), 0)),
  Basis = c("assumption", "assumption", "planted", "assumption", "convention", "assumption", "assumption", "convention"))
knitr::kable(tab)
```

::: {.reader-note}
**How to read the table.** Each row is a setting that shapes the results. The last column
says whether it is an analyst's assumption, a standard convention, or a feature planted in
the synthetic data.

**What the table tells you.** Most settings are assumptions. Changing the windows, risk
bands or deletion budget would change the reported numbers, so each is recorded in one place.
:::

## Limitations

- **Synthetic data.** Confounding, regime shift and overconfidence are planted. Real use needs NorthPoint's vendor-month panel, incident definition and dated SOC 2 reports.
- **Few events.** `r readRDS("data/calibration.rds")$n_eval_incidents` evaluation incidents and 18 forecast months limit power; more history could change pages 2 and 3.
- **Thin overlay window.** Six months and `r readRDS("data/calibration.rds")$n_fit_incidents` incidents is little. A real overlay needs a refit schedule and tolerances set in advance.
- **Information timing.** Start-of-month availability of patch latency and financial health is assumed; real feeds need timestamps.
- **One dataset.** Seed 34 was chosen in development; the seed sweep on page 4 checks repeatability only.
- **Partial validation.** Scores and outcomes only; the vendor's internals stay unseen.
